events.title: VALERIUS OPENS THE ESTATE FOR A PRIVATE ARMORY
events.body: Valerius orders the estate mines, metal stores, smithies, and finishing workshops placed at the service of a single commission: armor and weapons worthy of the men who now stand closest to him. The work uses materials already belonging to his personal holdings, so no new purchase, sale, or treasury expenditure is realized. Valerius personally inspects the metal and rejects pieces that fail his standards for consistency, balance, or finish. The finest smiths living and working on the estate are brought together under one commission. What begins as equipment production becomes a deliberate attempt to give the guard a recognizable material identity while remaining unmistakably Roman in form.

events.title: ROMAN FORMS, VALERIAN MATERIALS
events.body: The armorers retain the recognizable Roman language of the equipment: articulated protection, practical helmets, reinforced fittings, and equipment intended for field use rather than ceremony. The materials come from Valerius's own high-quality reserves, giving the finished pieces unusual consistency and refinement. Smiths, leatherworkers, and finishers fit the equipment individually to each guard member. The hundred guards therefore receive armor traditional in silhouette but unmistakably belonging to Valerius's household. The equipment register is expanded without changing the expedition's manpower.

events.title: EACH GUARD RECEIVES ARMOR FITTED TO HIS OWN METHOD
events.body: Valerius refuses to make the personal guard identical at the expense of function. Each of the one hundred men receives armor fitted around his established fighting method, with individual sizing, reinforcement, shield fittings, helmet adjustments, and weapon accommodation recorded by name. Infantry equipment permits disciplined foot movement while cavalry protection allows mounted movement without abandoning the Roman character. The twenty newly admitted veterans are fitted alongside Valerius's established veterans with no distinction in workmanship. Their equipment becomes another expression of the principle established in the previous round: individual excellence remains intact while the whole guard functions as one body.

events.title: THE SMITHS FORGE VALERIUS'S OWN PANOPLY
events.body: Valerius reserves the finest completed materials for himself and personally supervises the final assembly of his own equipment. His armor follows the traditional Roman style but is more carefully finished and reinforced, with every major component fitted specifically to his body and accustomed movement. It is practical protection rather than a parade costume. His weapon set is completed beside the armor so the pieces form one coherent personal kit. The estate smiths understand that they are making equipment that will accompany Valerius into whatever campaigns follow.

events.title: THE GLADIUS AND DOUBLE-REINFORCED PILUM
events.body: Valerius selects a high-quality Roman gladius as his principal sidearm and a double-reinforced pilum as his personal throwing weapon. The pilum is treated as a personal weapon rather than replaceable issue equipment, with its construction reinforced by the estate smiths while retaining its Roman character. Valerius orders its history to remain visible: every confirmed shield he personally pierced receives its own permanent mark in the weapon's record. The marks are treated as a living campaign record rather than decoration. No encounter is added unless it belongs to Valerius's established history.

events.title: THE SHIELDS BECOME A CHRONICLE OF SURVIVAL
events.body: While examining the completed pilum and his new shield, Valerius has the smiths and record-keepers assemble the surviving testimony of his previous fighting. Each confirmed shield-piercing receives its own place in the weapon's record without inventing names or circumstances that the campaign record does not establish. The scars, notches, and inscriptions become a visible chronology of participation and survival. The guards understand that their commander's equipment carries physical evidence of the battles through which he has actually lived. Several veterans begin discussing their own equipment as objects that should preserve truthful memories rather than merely display wealth. No new battle occurs, but the armory becomes a place where the expedition's memory is materially preserved.

events.title: THE PERSONAL GUARD STANDS IN ITS NEW PANOPLY
events.body: The hundred-man personal guard appears together in its newly completed equipment, Roman in overall form but unified by the exceptional materials and craftsmanship of Valerius's estate. Individual weapons and fittings remain distinct while the armor gives the guard a common visual language. Valerius joins them wearing his completed panoply, gladius at his side and double-reinforced pilum carried as a personal record of the battles he has survived. The guard does not become ceremonial: the equipment is immediately treated as working field gear maintained by the estate workshops. The result is a household tradition taking physical form, with every man equipped according to his role.
